To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the carrier-envelope phase (CEP) sensitivity of multiphotion photoelectron emission from metals can be enhanced by a proper choice of the laser intensity, the number of involved photons, and the pulse duration.
the carrier-envelope phase of ultrashort laser fields is directly measured with high precision by using the photoemission from a polycrystal surface of gold.
the carrier-envelope phase of few-cycle pulses is not directly measured by the photoemission signal from metal surfaces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of ultrafast electron dynamics in metal surfaces and their interaction with few-cycle laser pulses.
the ultrafast dynamics and the carrier-envelope phase sensitivity in the multiphoton photoionization of solid surfaces.
ultrafast dynamics in solids induced by few-cycle laser fields and with the carrier-envelope phase sensitivity in photoemission processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in general, the carrier-envelope phase sensitivity is determined by the ratio of the electron lifetime to the laser period, and the carrier-envelope phase can only be detected if this ratio is of the order of unity.
the carrier-envelope phase sensitivity is a very complex function of the laser intensity, the pulse duration and the material properties.
the phase dependence of the electron yield from a metal surface depends on the surface properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phase dependence of photoemission is strongly influenced by the dynamics of the electrons.
the carrier-envelope phase sensitivity is strongly influenced by the ultrafast dynamics of the photoemitted electron.
the carrier-envelope phase is an important parameter for the control of ultrafast processes in solids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the carrier-envelope phase of a short laser pulse is not a constant but can be modulated by the surface material.
the carrier-envelope phase of the driving pulse has a significant influence on the photoelectron energy spectrum.
the carrier-envelope phase sensitivity can be enhanced by increasing the number of photons involved in the photoemission and by increasing the laser intensity.
